claims.text: The overall response rate to UK Biobank recruitment was 5.5%.
The response rate to UK Biobank recruitment was higher in women.
The response rate to UK Biobank recruitment was higher in older age groups.
The response rate to UK Biobank recruitment was higher in individuals from less socioeconomically deprived areas.
UK Biobank participants were less likely to be obese compared with the general population.
UK Biobank participants were less likely to smoke compared with the general population.
UK Biobank participants were less likely to drink alcohol on a daily basis compared with the general population.
UK Biobank participants reported fewer self-reported diseases compared with the general population.
Total cancer incidence rates at ages 65–69 were 31% lower in men in UK Biobank compared with the national population.
Total cancer incidence rates at ages 65–69 were 42% lower in women in UK Biobank compared with the national population.
All-cause mortality at ages 65–69 in UK Biobank was 56.0% lower in men compared to national death rates.
All-cause mortality at ages 65–69 in UK Biobank was 67.6% lower in women compared to national death rates.

methodologies.name: Cross-sectional comparison with representative population surveys
methodologies.description: Comparison of sociodemographic, physical, lifestyle, and health-related characteristics of 503,310 UK Biobank participants against 8,761,869 invitees and nationally representative data sources matched by age, sex, geography, and period of collection.
datasets: Office for National Statistics cancer incidence and mortality data
conditions: Participants aged 40–69 recruited between 2006 and 2010 in England, Wales, and Scotland

limitations.text: UK Biobank is not representative of the general population on a variety of sociodemographic, physical, lifestyle and health-related characteristics, with evidence of a 'healthy volunteer' selection bias.
UK Biobank is not suitable for deriving generalizable disease prevalence and incidence rates.
